title.rendered: UAE announces new tax changes set to take effect in coming months

content.rendered:
UAE businesses face two federal tax updates covering electronic smoking products, and UAE businesses face revised financial reporting after new Ministry of Finance decisions in August 2026.

Vape liquid suppliers must apply a new minimum excise price from September 1 2026. Businesses face revised financial reporting requirements from October 1 after the Ministry of Finance introduced updated corporate tax rules covering audited financial statements.

Both measures alter tax calculations and compliance planning for affected operators. Ministry of Finance legislation confirms Cabinet Decision No. 137 of 2026 covers the new excise pricing requirement.

Vape liquid excise price changes from September

Ministry of Finance rules introduce a minimum excise price of $0.27 (AED1) per millilitre for liquids used in electronic smoking devices.

September 1 2026 is the effective date. UAE authorities announced the measure on August 6 2026.

Electronic smoking liquids remain subject to a 100 per cent excise tax rate. Cabinet Decision No. 197 of 2025 confirms that rate for both liquids and electronic smoking devices.

A 60 millilitre bottle consequently carries a minimum excise base of $16.34 (AED60). Operators then apply the existing 100 per cent rate against the applicable excise price.

Ministry of Finance rules retain existing minimum excise pricing for cigarette rolls, waterpipe tobacco, ready-to-use tobacco and similar products.

Importers and retailers face pricing adjustments

Importers, manufacturers and distributors need to review product records before September 1 as the minimum price changes taxable values across lower-priced liquids.

Retailers also need to assess inventory pricing where bottles carry an excise value below $0.27 (AED1) per millilitre.

Cabinet Decision No. 137 of 2026 sets the legal basis for the revised calculation. Ministry of Finance records list the decision among UAE tax legislation issued during 2026.

UAE authorities designed the requirement to standardise excise treatment across tobacco and electronic smoking categories.

Ministry officials also linked the decision to stronger compliance and reduced practices that weaken effective tax collection.

Federal Tax Authority guidance confirms electronic smoking liquids and devices remain within the UAE excise tax system at a 100 per cent rate.

Revenue threshold applies to taxable businesses

From October 1, businesses operating through several UAE entities will need accounting records capable of supporting group-level reporting. Finance teams must maintain consistent transaction classification, reconciliation and corporate tax records across participating companies.

Ministerial Decision No. 84 replaces previous audit rules for tax periods beginning from January 1 2025. Earlier provisions continue to cover periods starting before that date.

Taxable persons outside a tax group must prepare audited financial statements when revenue exceeds $13.6 million (AED50 million) during a relevant tax period.

Qualifying Free Zone Persons must also prepare and maintain audited financial statements. Their requirement applies regardless of the $13.6m (AED50m) revenue threshold.

Vanhee said the exemption largely disappears in practice, because it stops applying altogether once a business buys more than AED 100,000 in total from one supplier over a year. That works out to around AED 8,300 a month.

Revenue calculations for non-resident persons use income derived through UAE permanent establishments or UAE nexuses.

Companies approaching the threshold will need accurate revenue recognition throughout each reporting period. Accounting teams must establish whether revenue exceeds the statutory level and retain supporting financial records.

Audit preparation also affects filing schedules, year-end controls and corporate tax reporting processes.

Free zone businesses face separate requirements

Qualifying Free Zone Persons distributing goods or materials in or from a Designated Zone face additional procedural requirements.

Federal Tax Authority procedures will govern compliance requirements for distribution businesses operating within the Corporate Tax Free Zone regime.

Distribution companies must align accounting records with qualifying activity requirements and Designated Zone transactions. Finance teams will need transaction-level evidence covering relevant goods, counterparties and revenue streams.

Businesses operating across free zones, mainland entities and tax groups must classify each entity correctly before determining its audit requirement.

Ministerial Decision No. 84 applies to tax periods starting on or after January 1 2025. Companies with different financial year dates must determine which rules govern each reporting period.

title.rendered: Tony Robbins to bring his Breakthrough event to Dubai in GCC first

content.rendered:
Tony Robbins will bring his Breakthrough leadership and personal-performance event to Dubai in 2027, marking the programme’s first appearance in the GCC.

The best-selling author, investor and business strategist will appear at Coca-Cola Arena on April 24, 2027, for a four-hour event aimed at entrepreneurs, executives, investors and business leaders.

Registration for the ticket presale has opened through the Coca-Cola Arena website, although ticket prices have not yet been disclosed.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Coca-Cola Arena (@cocacolaarena)

The one-day event is being presented by Locker Room Events and has been created specifically for a Middle Eastern audience, according to its organisers.

Breakthrough will combine business and leadership advice with storytelling, live coaching, guided exercises, large-scale visuals and music.

Organisers said the event would focus on decision-making, leadership, business growth, wealth creation, relationships and personal performance.

It is being marketed primarily towards people who have already achieved a degree of professional or financial success but want to identify opportunities for further growth.

“Dubai is home to some of the most ambitious entrepreneurs and leaders in the world,” Robbins said.

“I’m excited to bring Breakthrough to the UAE and connect with leaders and entrepreneurs who are ready to challenge their limits and create the next level of impact in their lives and businesses.

“Your breakthrough begins the moment you decide.”

Middle East business leaders

The Dubai event is expected to attract C-suite executives, founders, investors, high-net-worth individuals and decision-makers from the financial and property sectors.

A limited number of Royal and VIP packages will be released during the presale period.

The premium packages will include priority entry, exclusive merchandise, recognition as a founding attendee and the opportunity to have a meet-and-greet photograph with Robbins. Full details and prices have yet to be announced.

Robbins has spent more than four decades building a business around live events, coaching programmes, books and digital content.

He is the author of eight international bestsellers, including Money: Master the Game, Unshakeable and Life Force.

The organisers claim more than 100 million people across 195 countries have participated in his events, coaching services and digital platforms. The figure has not been independently verified.

Robbins also serves as chairman of a holding company comprising more than 110 privately owned businesses, which he says collectively generate annual revenue exceeding $9 billion.

His previous clients and collaborators have included athletes Serena Williams and Andre Agassi, Salesforce founder Marc Benioff and the Golden State Warriors basketball team.

The announcement adds another major business and motivational event to Dubai’s live-entertainment calendar as promoters increasingly target the region’s growing population of entrepreneurs, senior executives and wealthy investors.

title.rendered: Shipping giant loses $600mn in three months due to Middle East conflict

content.rendered:
Shipping giant Hapag-Lloyd incurred around $600 million (AED 2.20 billion) in additional Q2 costs from regional maritime disruption.

Quarterly profit returned to $83 million (AED 304.8 million) as transport volumes and spot rates strengthened. Hapag-Lloyd reported Q2 group EBITDA of $829 million (AED 3.04 billion), slightly above the prior-year quarter.

Hamburg carrier Hapag-Lloyd attributed most additional expenditure to higher bunker costs. Insurance, storage, inland transport and service rerouting added further expense.

Alternative routings kept cargo moving across Gulf markets. Hapag-Lloyd deployed land bridges for Upper Gulf supply chains and continued serving customers through revised inland and feeder connections.

Q2 earnings recover as shipping volumes strengthen

Hapag-Lloyd generated $5.84 billion (AED 21.45 billion) in group revenue during Q2 2026. Group EBIT reached $176 million (AED 646.4 million).

Q1 had closed with a group loss of $256 million (AED 940.2 million), following weather disruption and regional shipping constraints. Q2 returned Hapag-Lloyd to quarterly profitability as cargo demand accelerated.

Asian exports and stronger US demand drove much of that recovery. Container volumes increased to 3.5 million TEU from 3.4 million TEU during Q2 2025.

Average freight rates climbed 9 per cent year on year to $1,475 (AED 5,417) per TEU. Q2 2025 rates stood at $1,354 (AED 4,972) per TEU.

Hapag-Lloyd’s Gemini network also maintained high schedule reliability during operational disruption. Carrier management identified network reliability as an important contributor to service continuity during the quarter.

UAE gateways support Upper Gulf cargo continuity

UAE logistics infrastructure forms a central part of Hapag-Lloyd’s contingency routing for Upper Gulf cargo.

Hapag-Lloyd reopened bookings to and from Upper Gulf locations through hinterland connections and third-party feeder services in July. UAE-bound containers can transship through Fujairah or Khorfakkan before continuing by land bridge to their final destination.

Cargo destined for Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar and Bahrain can follow another UAE corridor. Containers move through Fujairah or Khorfakkan before road transfer to Jebel Ali or Sharjah.

Intra-Gulf feeder services then provide onward connections to final destinations.

Fujairah and Khorfakkan also provide links to ports in Oman and India, connecting regional cargo with Hapag-Lloyd’s mainline network. Bonded transport between Fujairah or Khorfakkan and Jebel Ali or Sharjah takes about five days.

Hapag-Lloyd also confirmed that its Upper Gulf land bridges were maintaining customer supply chains despite higher operating expenditure.

Liner business absorbs higher operating expenditure

Hapag-Lloyd’s liner shipping division generated Q2 revenue of $5.68 billion (AED 20.86 billion).

Segment EBITDA reached $773 million (AED 2.84 billion), while EBIT totalled $153 million (AED 561.9 million). Regional route constraints increased bunker, insurance, storage, rerouting and inland transport expenditure.

Terminal and Infrastructure operations recorded stronger revenue growth.

Quarterly revenue reached $191 million (AED 701.4 million), supported by the consolidation of J M Baxi’s container business and Latin American volume growth. EBITDA reached $55 million (AED 202 million).

Hapag-Lloyd operated 300 container ships with total transport capacity of 2.5 million TEU at its August reporting date. Carrier operations covered 129 liner services linking 600 ports globally.

Hapag-Lloyd raises 2026 earnings outlook

Hapag-Lloyd raised its full-year earnings outlook on July 13 after Q2 trading conditions strengthened.

Group EBITDA guidance stands between $2.7 billion (AED 9.92 billion) and $3.7 billion (AED 13.59 billion). Group EBIT guidance ranges from $100 million (AED 367.3 million) to $1.1 billion (AED 4.04 billion).

H1 transport volume reached 6.68 million TEU, up from 6.59 million TEU during the comparable 2025 period.

Hapag-Lloyd enters the second half with higher Q2 volumes, firmer freight rates and expanded routing options across Gulf markets. UAE gateways remain integrated into contingency flows serving Upper Gulf customers and connecting regional cargo with wider mainline services.

title.rendered: Dubai advertising deals hit $408m as 683 assets tendered and Metro naming rights expand: Mada Media

content.rendered:
Dubai’s out-of-home (OOH) advertising sector recorded approximately AED1.5bn ($408m) in signed contracts during the first half of 2026, covering 683 advertising assets across the emirate.

Mada Media said 80 local and regional advertising companies participated in tenders during the period, while two new naming rights agreements were signed for stations on the Dubai Metro Red Line, including one with a global brand for the first time.

Mada Media, the company responsible for organising, developing and managing Dubai’s OOH advertising sector, said investment activity increased during the first half of the year.

The tenders covered 683 digital and non-digital advertising assets and attracted participation from 80 local and regional advertising companies.

They also included agreements to convert a significant proportion of existing assets into digital formats using the latest technologies in advertising displays and in line with internationally recognised safety standards.

Dubai advertising deals

Advertising assets tendered included 27 digital Unipoles and 20 Bridge Banners, comprising six digital and 14 static assets.

Four static Hoardings were also included, alongside a number of advertising displays on lighting poles and flags.

The assets are distributed across key areas of Dubai and major high-traffic roads.

Mada Media also signed two naming rights agreements for stations on the Dubai Metro Red Line during the first half of 2026.

One agreement is with a local brand, while the second is, for the first time, with one of the world’s leading global brands. Further details are due to be announced.

Mada Media oversees naming rights agreements for stations on both the Green and Red Lines of Dubai Metro.

Dubai Metro Station naming

The company described Metro station naming rights as one of its most prominent investment products, attracting interest and demand from local, regional and global brands.

Matar Al Tayer, Chairman of Mada Media, said the first-half results reflected the strength of Dubai’s OOH advertising sector and growing confidence among local and regional investors and companies.

He said: “The participation of 80 local and regional advertising companies in the tenders launched by the company is an indication of the expanding investor base and strong demand for the investment opportunities offered by the sector. It also confirms the success of the approach adopted by Mada Media in managing and developing the OOH advertising ecosystem based on principles that balance enhancing the economic viability of assets, providing high-quality opportunities for the private sector, and elevating the quality of Dubai’s urban landscape.”

Mada Media’s next phase will include further development of an integrated model for the OOH advertising sector, including deploying modern technologies and accelerating the transition towards digital advertising assets.

The company is also seeking to adopt new solutions designed to enhance the efficiency and investment value of advertising assets while maintaining safety, sustainability and quality standards.

Mada Media expansion

Its updated strategy focuses on expanding investment opportunities, attracting new categories of investors and diversifying advertising assets and solutions.

Mada Media is also exploring opportunities to use the expertise and model it has developed to expand into new markets as it seeks to build a model for managing and developing the OOH advertising sector at regional and global levels.

Mansoor Al Sabahi, CEO of Mada Media, said: “The results achieved during the first half of 2026 confirm the company’s successful implementation of its plans to develop and support the growth of a more efficient and sustainable OOH advertising ecosystem.

“This is demonstrated by the strong interest from local and regional advertising companies in the diverse investment opportunities being offered, as well as the variety of advertising assets included in these tenders, which provided investors with opportunities to diversify and develop their investments by encouraging the digitalisation of a large number of these assets and promoting the use of the latest technologies and programmatic advertising, which will bring significant transformation to the OOH advertising market in the coming period.”

Dubai Metro Green and Red Line opportunities

Mada Media is seeking to expand naming rights agreements for stations on both the Green and Red Lines of Dubai Metro.

Al Sabahi said: “Our efforts are currently focused on supporting digital transformation across the sector by adopting the latest technologies in advertising screens, supporting its growth and business continuity by providing support and assistance to local companies and enabling global companies to expand their business networks in the local market. We are also expanding naming rights agreements for stations on the Green and Red Lines of Dubai Metro, which are overseen by Mada Media and represent some of the rarest and most important investment opportunities in the OOH advertising sector.

“These opportunities provide sustainable, long-term added value for investors and strengthen the position of both local and global brands within the emirate’s community.”

Mada Media also launched an exclusive tender for emerging national advertising companies that are members of the Mohammed Bin Rashid Establishment for Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Dubai SME).

A total of 18 emerging national advertising companies participated in the tender, which was launched by Mada Media for the first time.

The initiative is intended to strengthen their presence and competitiveness, enable them to secure a share of returns from the OOH advertising market and support their growth and sustainability.

Mada Media develops Dubai advertising ecosystem

Mada Media said it has focused since its establishment on developing a regulatory and operational ecosystem based on transparency, streamlined procedures and efficiency in managing and operating advertising assets.

Al Sabahi said: “Since the company was established, we have focused on building a regulatory and operational ecosystem based on transparency, streamlined procedures, and enhanced efficiency in the management and operation of advertising assets.

“This approach seeks to balance support for investment with preserving the emirate’s visual identity and the quality of its urban landscape, in line with sustainable development objectives and Dubai’s vision for the future.”

During the first half of the year, Mada Media also introduced initiatives aimed at supporting partners and investors, improving business resilience and continuity, and enabling companies to grow.

The company’s strategy centres on innovation, digital transformation, expanding investment opportunities and strengthening strategic partnerships, with its development plans supporting the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan.

title.rendered: Elon Musk’s SpaceX moves into natural-gas trading with new specialist team

content.rendered:
Elon Musk’s SpaceX is assembling its own natural-gas trading operation as the company’s demand for fuel and electricity grows across rocket launches, manufacturing and new infrastructure projects.

The company is recruiting a natural-gas trader to establish and lead a new team responsible for buying, selling and managing energy commodities.

According to the official job advertisement, the operation will handle both physical gas supplies and financial trading.

The successful candidate will be expected to originate, structure and execute transactions while developing strategies designed to reduce supply risk, control costs and potentially profit from movements and inefficiencies in energy markets.

The trader will also manage positions in response to changes in weather, fuel demand, emissions policy, regulation and market conditions.

Significantly, the team will maintain its own profit-and-loss statement. This suggests that SpaceX is creating something closer to a commercial trading desk than a conventional corporate procurement function.

There is currently no indication that SpaceX intends to offer energy-trading services to outside customers. The immediate objective appears to be securing reliable and competitively priced gas for its expanding operations.

SpaceX enters energy trading

The move reflects Musk’s long-standing preference for vertical integration: bringing strategically important capabilities inside his companies rather than depending entirely on outside suppliers.

SpaceX already designs and manufactures much of its rocket and satellite technology. It is now applying a similar approach to the fuel and electricity needed to support those operations.

Natural gas is particularly important to the company because Starship, its giant reusable rocket, uses supercooled liquid methane combined with liquid oxygen as propellant.

As SpaceX attempts to increase the frequency of Starship launches, its requirement for methane and the infrastructure needed to transport, process and store it will grow substantially.

SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell has previously said the company is considering building pipelines and potentially drilling for its own gas. Those plans would take the business considerably deeper into the energy supply chain.

Other vacancies support the impression that a wider operation is taking shape. SpaceX has also advertised for specialists covering gas procurement, pipeline infrastructure and energy and commodities transactions.

Building a trading team

The newly advertised trader will recruit and manage a small team of traders and analysts while developing relationships with producers, pipeline operators, brokers and other market counterparties.

Candidates must have at least four years of relevant experience in areas such as natural-gas trading, energy-market analysis, cost control, engineering or commodity finance.

The position is based at Cape Canaveral in Florida and cannot be performed remotely. International travel could occupy as much as half of the working week, while applicants must also be able to pass US Air Force background checks.

Experience of global gas markets, pipelines, storage, LNG and cryogenic commodities is listed among the preferred qualifications.

The role represents another example of the boundaries between technology, industrial manufacturing and energy becoming increasingly blurred.

Large technology companies require extraordinary amounts of power for artificial intelligence, data centres and advanced manufacturing. SpaceX additionally needs methane to fuel its rockets.

By creating an internal trading desk, the company could gain greater control over prices, supplies and operational risk while potentially turn its enormous energy requirements into another source of commercial advantage.

title.rendered: Dubai’s two airports to be connected by new 55km train line

content.rendered:
Dubai has received six consultant proposals for the planned 55km Airport Express Line linking Dubai International Airport with Al Maktoum International Airport.

Airport Express plans cover five stations and two branch alignments connecting major commercial and residential districts. Dubai’s Road and Transport Authority(RTA) has not confirmed a construction timetable or opening date for the proposed rail corridor.

Six groups compete for design contract

AECOM with Surbana Jurong, AtkinsRéalis, Jacobs, Parsons with Arup, Systra with Egis and WSP submitted proposals for the consultancy package.

RTA issued the tender during 2026 for study and design services covering the Airport Express Line. An initial June submission deadline was later shifted to July 8.

Tender documents place the line between DXB in Al Garhoud and DWC in Dubai South. Procurement remains focused on engineering studies and design work rather than a construction award.

RTA has not disclosed a contract value for the consultancy package.

Airport Express procurement runs separately from plans to extend Route 2020 from Expo City towards DWC. That extension covers about three kilometres and two stations under the scope reported during 2026.

Route connects DXB with JVC and Dubai South

Planned alignment starts at the existing Red Line Metro station serving DXB in Al Garhoud. Services would pass through Al Jaddaf before following the Al Khail Road corridor towards Jumeirah Village Circle.

Trains would continue from JVC towards Al Maktoum International Airport.

One branch would connect JVC with Al Fardan Exchange Metro Station near Emirates Golf Club. Another branch would run towards Business Bay, where a station forms part of the proposed alignment.

JVC also sits on Dubai Metro’s approved Gold Line, creating another interchange point within Dubai’s expanding rail network.

Gold Line plans cover 42 kilometres and 18 stations with investment of about $9.3 billion (AED34 billion). RTA has scheduled its inauguration for September 9 2032. Business Bay and JVC both form part of that alignment.

Stations add airport passenger processing

Airport Express station plans include remote airline check-in, baggage drop services and security screening facilities.

Those specifications place aviation processing within the rail journey rather than limiting stations to passenger boarding and interchange functions. Procurement documents include these facilities within the proposed passenger service scope.

RTA is expanding rail capacity as Metro passenger volumes continue to rise. Dubai Metro carried 295 million passengers during 2025, representing annual growth of 7 per cent.

Daily Metro usage averaged about one million passengers during the year. Metro services accounted for 40 per cent of public transport use across Dubai.

Blue Line construction provides another 30 kilometres of network capacity through 14 stations. RTA records construction progress at 10 per cent and expects completion to reach 30 per cent by the end of 2026.

Rail capacity aligns with DWC expansion

Dubai Airports recorded 95.2 million passengers at DXB during 2025, its highest annual traffic total. DXB currently connects passengers with 291 destinations through 108 international carriers.

DWC development carries an investment of $35 billion (AED128 billion), according to current Dubai Airports project information. Planned capacity reaches 150 million passengers annually during the next decade and ultimately exceeds 260 million.

Cargo capacity will reach 12 million tonnes annually at full development.

Dubai’s June 2026 airport development update specifies five parallel runways, two passenger terminals and seven concourses. More than 430 connected aircraft stands form part of the final configuration.

Current works cover packages for the Western Passenger Terminal, aircraft concourses, baggage handling infrastructure and an automated passenger transport system.

Airport plans also incorporate multimodal connections across air, rail and road networks, placing new rail capacity directly within DWC’s long-term transport requirements.

RTA has not announced a construction contract, final project cost or service launch date for the Airport Express Line.

title.rendered: UAE tax changes, 3-day weekend, new school rules, Kuwait visa update – 10 stories you missed this week

content.rendered:
Big changes are coming for UAE residents and businesses, with new tax rules, school requirements and VAT regulations taking effect in the weeks ahead.

A new minimum excise price for vaping liquids comes into force from September 1, while companies face tougher VAT refund rules from October.

Across the Gulf, public holidays and Kuwait visa changes are also approaching, with important dates for workers, residents and visitors.

Meanwhile, ambitious plans could revive the historic Hejaz Railway, potentially opening the door to future rail connectivity stretching from the GCC towards Türkiye. Plus, Dubai’s property market is showing renewed momentum, Sharjah is preparing for a new five-star hotel and Al Maktoum International Airport has issued an update on its massive inter-terminal train project.

Catch up on 10 of the biggest stories this week, as selected by Arabian Business editors.

UAE to introduce new tax from September 1

The UAE Ministry of Finance has confirmed that a new tax on electronic smoking devices will come into effect on September 1, 2026.

However, contrary to some beliefs it’s not the first time vapes and e-liquids have been subject to tax in the UAE. An excise tax on vapes and e-liquids was first introduced on December 1, 2019.

What is new about the tax being enforced next month is a minimum excise price for vaping liquids.

The Ministry of Finance announced the issuance of a decision on the minimum Excise Price for Tobacco Products and Liquids used in Electronic Smoking Devices and Tools. The decision aims to enhance the effectiveness of excise tax implementation and support compliance with the UAE’s tax legislation.

Under the rules and regulations of the new tax being introduced, the existing minimum Excise Price will continue to apply to Cigarettes, Water Pipe Tobacco, ready-to-use tobacco products, and similar products. The new tax will pave the way for the introduction of a minimum Excise Price of AED 1 per millilitre (mL) for Liquids used in Electronic Smoking Devices and Tools.

UAE 3-day weekend confirmed as Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain announce August holidays

The UAE, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain have confirmed August holidays to mark the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), with dates and days off varying across the Gulf.

Workers following standard working weeks in the UAE, Kuwait and Oman will benefit from three consecutive days off, while Bahrain has announced a Tuesday, August 25 holiday for ministries, state departments and public institutions.

See the confirmed holiday dates here.

UAE announces new school rules and gives parents two weeks to make major decision

The UAE’s Ministry of Education has introduced seven new requirements for students and parents when selecting an academic path, as the 2026-2027 school year begins on August 31.

The rules, published in the ministry’s official curriculum guide, apply to students in both public and private schools that follow the UAE curriculum.

Four of the responsibilities apply to students, and three to parents. Officials say the changes are designed to link school subject choices more directly to university admission requirements and future careers.

Students will have a two-week window after the start of term to switch between academic paths if they wish to change their choice.

Under the new guidance, students must attend workshops held by their school that explain the study paths on offer and what each one involves.

UAE announces major new rules for businesses starting from October 1

Businesses in the United Arab Emirates are being told to start checking up on their suppliers, or risk losing money they’re owed back from the tax authorities.

From October 1, the UAE’s Federal Tax Authority (FTA) will be able to refuse to refund VAT to a business if the goods or services it bought were linked, anywhere along the supply chain, to tax evasion.

VAT is a 5 per cent charge added to most goods and services in the UAE, introduced in 2018. Businesses normally claim back the VAT they’ve paid on their own purchases but under the new rules, that claim can now be blocked.

Legal experts say the toughest part of the new rule is that businesses no longer need to have known about wrongdoing to be penalised.

Thomas Vanhee, a partner at tax firm Aurifer Middle East, said if a business genuinely knew its purchase was tied to tax evasion, the refund refusal is automatic.

From Dubai to Istanbul by rail? The 120-year-old route making a comeback

Completed in stages between 1900 and 1908, the Hejaz Railway Line (HRL) created a direct rail connection between Damascus and Madinah.

Upon its completion, Hajj journeys that had previously taken around 40 days by camel could now be completed in five. For the Ottoman Empire the line offered not only faster pilgrimage but a peninsula spanning vein serving commerce, administration and military movement across its Arabian territories.

Over a hundred years on, the HRL has returned to focus to address ever growing maritime insecurity. Türkiye, Syria and Saudi Arabia are examining rail connectivity along the former route, while the UAE and Oman have emerged in discussions around possible extensions into the GCC Railway project.

Several transport agreements have been concluded over the past year concerning this, including a railway cooperation agreement between Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. No construction programme has yet emerged, but the agreement establishes significant political willingness.

Ottoman Sultan Abdulhamid II commissioned the Hejaz Railway project in 1900 under the guise of pilgrimage. Its value however, stretched further, giving the Ottoman administration a faster means of transporting soldiers, government officials and supplies into Arabia, reducing the time and difficulty involved in reaching territories far from the imperial heartland.

Kuwait visa rules change from September 1: What visitors and residents abroad need to know

Kuwait will end exceptional measures covering visit visas and absence permits for residents abroad from September 1, 2026, bringing temporary immigration arrangements introduced earlier this year to a close.

The Ministry of Interior said exceptional renewals applying to visit entry visas will stop and statutory periods will resume, while residents outside Kuwait will again be subject to the legal periods governing absence from the country.

The Ministry of Interior said that from September 1 it will stop applying exceptional renewal arrangements to all types of visit entry visas.

Instead, the statutory periods governing entry visas will resume in accordance with the applicable regulations and procedures.

The change brings an end to exceptional measures introduced earlier in 2026 that provided automatic extensions for visitors affected by the circumstances at the time.

UAE’s Gargash rejects claims of visa cancellations and Iran funding

Dr Anwar Gargash, Diplomatic Adviser to the UAE President, has rejected claims involving labour residency cancellations and financial facilities to Iran.

Gargash addressed the reports on X on August 19. He described the information as false and linked its circulation to what he called “desperate media campaigns”. His comments came as the UAE continued work around regional developments and planning for the period ahead.

Gargash said the UAE would answer such reports through measurable work and tangible results. “Facts and concrete achievements remain stronger than rumours, and work remains stronger than noise,” he wrote.

Gargash specifically addressed reports concerning the cancellation of labour residencies in the UAE. He rejected the information and identified it as part of a wider circulation of inaccurate claims.

His intervention also covered claims that financial facilities were being provided to Iran. Gargash rejected that information as untrue.

First 5-star hotel set to open in Sharjah

Emaar Hospitality Group will open Vida Aljada in Sharjah before the end of 2026, expanding its Vida Hotels and Resorts portfolio in the UAE.

Vida Aljada will operate as a five-star lifestyle hotel within Aljada’s Naseej District. Emaar Hospitality will manage the property as part of a four-building hospitality and residential complex developed by Arada.

Arada confirmed completion of the wider complex on April 9 2026. The development contains 175 hotel rooms, 149 serviced apartments and 255 branded residences.

Vida Aljada will introduce 175 rooms alongside suites and accommodation designed for longer stays. Guests will access dining, social and wellness facilities within the property.

Emaar Hospitality positions Vida as its upscale lifestyle hotel brand, with properties operating across the UAE and Bahrain. Vida Aljada carries a five-star rating within Emaar Hospitality’s booking system.

Dubai’s Al Maktoum International Airport issues update on world’s largest inter-terminal train

L&T and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries have landed the contract for Al Maktoum International Airport.

L&T, is a business unit of transportation infrastructure, has won the race to design and build what will be the world’s biggest airport after completion.

L&T and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) will be tasked with the responsibility of building the Automated People Mover (APM) system for Phase 1 of Al Maktoum International Airport, which will be located in Dubai.

The landmark project is being developed by Dubai Aviation City Corporation and will be implemented by Dubai Aviation Engineering Projects.

Once fully developed, Al Maktoum International Airport will become the world’s largest airport, with a capacity of 260 million passengers and 12 million tonnes of freight annually.

Dubai property market rebounds as sales rise and investors return

Dubai’s residential property market saw sale transactions rise, a pause in price reductions and the return of buyers, according to the latest data from Property Finder and Mortgage Finder.

Activity was largely concentrated within the secondary segment as well as apartments. Investors have seemingly returned through the mid-market, seeking value in homes before pricing stabilises higher.

Speaking on the matter was Cherif Sleiman, Chief Revenue Officer at Property Finder, who summarised July’s market behaviour as “a market that has moved back into growth, with transaction volumes and values rising together and buyers returning with real intent […] we expect that momentum to carry through the second half of the year.”

Looking at the numbers, sale transaction volumes rose from 8,887 in June to 9,217 in July, a climb of 3.8 per cent. Transaction value climbed 5.2 per cent from AED 33.2 billion to AED 34.9 billion.

This increase came near entirely from the secondary market, which saw volumes grow roughly 18 per cent from 4,100 to 4,800. This figure suggests an appetite for ready stock. Commercial activity volume grew a substantial 24.8 per cent to 397 deals, achieving a value of AED 5.8 billion.

title.rendered: UAE weather alert: Heavy rain possible as NCM forecasts rainfall, mist and 45kmph winds

content.rendered:
The UAE’s National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather alert for Saturday, warning that convective clouds could bring light to moderate rainfall that may become heavy at times across parts of the country.

Further rainfall is possible on Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday, according to the NCM’s forecast, while winds could reach 45kmph by Wednesday and conditions over the coming days could also include mist and blowing dust and sand.

UAE heavy rain alert issued on Saturday

The NCM alert is in effect from 1.30pm until 9pm on Saturday.

The weather conditions are expected to affect some eastern, southern and western areas of the UAE, extending to parts of the country’s interior.

The NCM warned of the possibility of convective cloud formation accompanied by light to moderate rainfall, which may become heavy at times.

The authority has also urged the public to follow safety measures during rain.

Motorists are advised to avoid driving unless absolutely necessary and, when driving is required, to proceed with caution and remain vigilant to ensure the safety of all road users.

Drivers should turn on low-beam headlights when visibility is reduced.

The NCM also urged people to follow weather forecasts through official channels in the UAE, comply with instructions issued by relevant authorities and avoid spreading rumours.

UAE weather forecast for Sunday, August 23

Conditions on Sunday, August 23 are forecast to be fair to partly cloudy, with a probability of convective clouds forming in eastern areas during the afternoon accompanied by rainfall.

Conditions will become humid during the night and on Monday morning over some coastal areas, with a probability of mist formation.

Light to moderate southeasterly to northeasterly winds are forecast, freshening at times and causing blowing dust. Wind speeds will range from 10-25kmph, reaching 40kmph.

The sea will be slight in the Arabian Gulf and Oman Sea.

Monday, August 24: Mist possible

Monday is expected to be fair to partly cloudy, with a probability of some convective clouds forming eastward during the afternoon.

Conditions will become humid at night and on Tuesday morning over some coastal areas, with a probability of mist formation.

Light to moderate southeasterly to northeasterly winds will freshen at times, with speeds of 10-25kmph, reaching 35kmph. The sea will remain slight in the Arabian Gulf and Oman Sea.

Tuesday, August 25: UAE rainfall and blowing dust forecast

Fair to partly cloudy conditions are forecast for Tuesday, with a probability of convective clouds forming eastward and southward during the afternoon accompanied by rainfall.

It will become humid at night and on Wednesday morning over some coastal areas.

Light to moderate southeasterly to northeasterly winds will freshen at times and cause blowing dust, with speeds of 10-25kmph, reaching 40kmph.

The sea will be slight in the Arabian Gulf and Oman Sea.

Wednesday, August 26: Winds could reach 45kmph

The NCM forecasts fair to partly cloudy conditions on Wednesday, with a chance of convective clouds forming eastward and southward during the afternoon accompanied by rainfall.

Light to moderate southeasterly to northeasterly winds are expected, becoming fresh to strong at times with clouds and causing blowing dust and sand.

Wind speeds will range from 15-30kmph, reaching 45kmph. The sea will remain slight in the Arabian Gulf and Oman Sea.

title.rendered: AI startup raises $20m to build ‘digital twins’ that copy office workers

content.rendered:
Saudi Aramco’s venture capital arm has co-led a $20 million investment in an AI startup building “digital twins” of office workers.

Twin1 AI emerged from stealth mode after completing the seed round, which was led by Aramco Ventures alongside Bessemer Venture Partners and Tribeca Venture Partners.

The San Mateo-based company is developing personalised AI versions of employees that can draw on their emails, meetings, documents and workplace applications.

Rather than operating as a general chatbot, each digital twin is designed to reflect the knowledge, working context, relationships and communication style of the employee it represents.

The technology can answer questions, locate information and perform approved tasks on an employee’s behalf. It works across platforms including Microsoft Teams, Slack, Outlook, Gmail, Google Drive and SharePoint.

Unlocking trapped value

Twin1’s founders believe the platform could help companies unlock valuable information currently trapped inside departments, inboxes and individual employees’ heads.

The investment also gives Aramco Ventures exposure to an emerging category of enterprise AI that could have applications across energy, financial services and other heavily regulated Gulf industries.

“Serving the world’s largest and most highly regulated enterprises requires far more than checking the standard security and compliance boxes,” said Daniel Carter, managing director of Aramco Ventures US.

“The Twin1 team of repeat founders combines a deep understanding of how these organisations operate and their AI governance needs with the experience required to make AI work in the enterprise.”

AI copies of employees

Digital twins have traditionally been virtual models of machinery, buildings and industrial systems. Engineers use them to monitor performance, predict failures and test possible changes without placing the physical asset at risk.

Twin1 is attempting to transfer that concept from equipment to people.

Every employee receives an AI model that continuously develops alongside their work. Individual twins can also communicate with one another, allowing the system to identify the right colleague, obtain authorised information and co-ordinate work across a company.

The concept raises obvious questions over privacy, security and responsibility, particularly when an AI system is authorised to communicate or act in someone’s name.

Twin1 said employees determine what information their twins can access and what may be shared with colleagues or other AI systems. Its platform uses six layers of controls combining company policies, existing permissions and human approval.

The company also offers private-cloud and single-tenant deployment options for organisations that do not want sensitive data placed within shared infrastructure.

Major law firms test Twin1

Twin1 said it has been testing the technology with businesses in regulated industries for more than a year.

Its customers include international law firms Linklaters, Orrick and Dechert, US lender Customers Bank and energy company Aegis Energy.

The company claims those early customers have used its technology to automate between 30 and 50 per cent of communications-related work. That figure has not been independently verified.

Orrick is both a customer and a strategic investor in the company.

Twin1 is also reported to have a pipeline containing more than 400 prospective customers. It plans eventually to introduce a self-service version aimed at smaller businesses and individual professionals, according to industry publication Artificial Lawyer.

The funding will be used to expand its teams in California and London, strengthen sales operations and continue developing the platform.

Twin1 was founded in 2025 by Lewis Liu, Tom Cahn, Huiting Liu and Jonathan Budd. Several members of the team previously worked at Eigen Technologies, an AI document-processing company acquired by contract-management platform Sirion in 2024.

Other participants in the funding round included EJF Ventures, F-Prime, Lakestar, Notion Capital, Tin Alley Ventures and several angel investors.

For Aramco Ventures, the deal extends its investment activity beyond industrial technologies and into software intended to reshape how large companies manage institutional knowledge.

The bigger test will be whether businesses trust an AI system not merely to assist their employees, but to represent them.

title.rendered: Four lessons from UAE property leaders for young real estate professionals

content.rendered:
Young professionals entering the UAE’s property industry must learn to think beyond launches and short-term sales if they want to build lasting careers, according to some of the country’s real estate executives.

The advice comes as the sector experiences one of its strongest periods of growth.

Dubai recorded AED252 billion in real estate transactions during the first quarter of 2026, an increase of 31 per cent from the corresponding period last year, according to Dubai Land Department data.

The market’s expansion is creating career opportunities across development, design, construction, finance, sales and property management.

However, it is also placing pressure on professionals to launch projects quickly, meet ambitious delivery schedules and satisfy increasingly demanding buyers.

Executives from AMWAJ Development, Meraki Group and Tomorrow World Properties said understanding investors, protecting reputations and designing around residents’ needs would be essential for the next generation.

Think like an investor

Young professionals should understand the full lifecycle of a development rather than specialising too early.

The advice from experts is quite simple: learn to think like an investor, not just a builder.

Real estate is often taught as a construction discipline, but the projects that succeed are the ones where every decision, from concept design to final handover, is tested against a single question: does this protect the value we promised our investors?

Experts encouraged new entrants to gain experience in development strategy, design management, regulatory approvals and construction delivery.

That breadth allows professionals to understand how decisions made during the feasibility stage affect the cost, quality and performance of a completed project several years later.

The advice is that discipline matters more than speed. The developments that hold their value long after handover are the ones built on rigorous planning and honest cost control, not shortcuts.

Design for people

Emad Saleh, founder and chairman of AMWAJ Development, warned against chasing scale without considering how people will use a property.

“The developments that endure, that hold their meaning as well as their value, are the ones shaped around real human experience rather than excess,” he said.

Saleh said design decisions should have a practical purpose, with layouts, materials and shared spaces planned around residents rather than added primarily for visual impact.

“Design should never be decorative,” he said. “I encourage anyone starting out to ask why a space is designed the way it is before asking how it looks.”

Sustainability should also be considered at the beginning of a project rather than added later as a marketing feature, he said.

Protect your reputation

Ajay Rajendran, founder and chairman of Meraki Group, identified reputation as the most important asset a young developer or entrepreneur can build.

“Your next opportunity is almost always earned by the quality of your last project,” he said.

“It’s easy to get caught up in launches, sales milestones and ambitious expansion plans, but none of those matter if you don’t consistently deliver on your promises.”

Rajendran said buyers remember whether developers complete properties on time, while investors assess whether projects retain value after handover.

He also advised young leaders to build multidisciplinary teams rather than attempting to control every decision themselves.

“When every function understands not only its own responsibilities but also how its decisions affect the next stage of the development lifecycle, challenges are identified earlier,” he said.

Look beyond the cycle

Xu Ma, founder and chairman of Tomorrow World Properties, said developers should consider the emotional effect buildings have on occupants.

“People remember how a space makes them feel long after they forget its specifications,” he said.

Ma identified natural light, access to outdoor space, practical layouts and community infrastructure as increasingly important to buyers.

He argued that developers should resist making decisions based solely on the current property cycle and instead consider how neighbourhoods will evolve over decades.

“Build for the life people want, not the cycle developers expect,” Ma said.

While Dubai’s expanding market offers considerable opportunities, the executives’ advice carries a common message: short-term success may generate a sale, but credibility, thoughtful design and disciplined delivery are what create a lasting property business.

excerpt.rendered: Executives explain why reputation, discipline and long-term thinking matter more than chasing rapid property growth

title.rendered: Iran warns of ‘devastating’ response to new US threats as oil prices rise on sanctions plan

content.rendered:
Iran said on Friday that its response to any new US threats would be “devastating” after Washington pledged to impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he would give details on Monday of the planned sanctions, after President Donald Trump warned of economic consequences against any country that provided “any type of lifeline to Iran.”

The chief of staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said the Islamic Republic’s reaction would be broad and decisive.

“With preparedness across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, Iran’s armed forces will respond to the enemy’s new threats with crushing, punishing and devastating responses,” Abdollahi was quoted as saying by Iranian media.

Iranian leaders and Trump alike have issued triumphant and threatening statements even as each side has yet to prevail in the war that the US and Israel started nearly six months ago, killing thousands of people while drawing in other Gulf nations and pushing up global fuel prices.

Iran threatens devastating response

US attacks have severely diminished Iran’s economy and its conventional forces, but Tehran maintains enough missile and drone capability to impede oil tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and attack regional rivals.

Trump, meanwhile, has yet to achieve objectives he set at the start of the war such as dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers. The war has driven up gas prices and weighed heavily on his popularity, which fell to the lowest point in his current term in a Reuters/Ipsos poll this week.

Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, the country’s main negotiator in mediated talks with the US, said Washington appeared to have concluded it could not prevail in its direct military confrontation.

“We must make plans to deal with the unjust sanctions so that we can overcome them,” he said in neighbouring Iraq.

But, speaking to regional business people late on Thursday, Qalibaf acknowledged the strain on Iran’s economy.

“No matter how much military power we have, we won’t survive if people are hungry and we don’t have financial turnover, economic growth and national production,” Qalibaf said, according to official news agency IRNA.

Oil prices increase

International and United States crude oil futures rose on Friday after the US threatened economic sanctions on trading partners, raising expectations of tighter supply in the coming weeks.

Bessent told CNBC he would provide details on the new sanctions at a press conference on Monday, adding, “We are going to collapse this regime.”

Iran has weathered near-continuous economic sanctions for nearly 50 years, since the Islamic Revolution of 1979, but its people are suffering high inflation, a weakening currency and energy shortages along with damaged infrastructure.

Tighter sanctions could have wider international implications. Bessent said China got half its energy from the Gulf so it would make sense for them to “get with the program.”

China buys more than 80 per cent of Iran’s shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler, but further US economic warfare with Beijing, which has eased earlier restrictions on exports of its vital rare-earth minerals, risks retaliation.

The Chinese embassy in Washington said, “Sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem” and called for diplomacy.

There are other significant risks, especially to US allies in the Gulf, some of whose energy facilities and the desalination plants they depend on for drinking water have come under Iranian attack.

The US and Iran have twice announced ceasefire deals, in April and June, aiming to restore the free flow of ships through Hormuz, which before February carried about a fifth of all traded oil.

Iran and Oman, which lies just across the narrow strait, have been in separate talks with a stated purpose to resume navigation, but the US has opposed any deal that would impose a toll on ships.

NATO’s top commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, convened a videoconference of allies at the chief of defence level on Wednesday to discuss ways to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, his spokesperson told Reuters on Friday.

The spokesperson said the effort was not a NATO mission but given the alliance’s capabilities, “it makes sense for NATO to facilitate in this way.”

title.rendered: Dubai airport passengers can cut customs procedures from 45 minutes to under 5

content.rendered:
Dubai airport passengers can reduce the time needed to complete customs procedures through the red channel from 45 minutes to less than five minutes using Dubai Customs’ iDeclare service, as authorities prepare for the post-summer travel peak.

Dubai Customs has deployed a comprehensive operational plan for returning residents and international visitors, with round-the-clock teams, increased staffing during peak periods, digital declaration tools and 77 baggage screening machines operating across Dubai’s air entry points.

The operational plan is designed to manage the influx of residents and international visitors returning to Dubai following the summer break.

Dubai Customs is increasing staffing levels in arrival halls and deploying personnel according to flight schedules and periods of peak demand.

Teams are also being reinforced in high-traffic areas, while the technical performance of screening equipment is being enhanced.

Dubai Customs prepares for peak airport arrivals

The measures are intended to manage passenger and baggage flows more efficiently and reduce the time between passengers arriving and completing customs procedures.

Customs teams operate around the clock at Dubai’s air entry points.

Dubai Customs’ technology infrastructure includes 77 baggage screening machines. Of these, 58 are used for checked and large baggage, while 19 are used for carry-on luggage. Additional inspection equipment also supports customs operations.

The screening system is designed to accelerate baggage checks and improve detection accuracy.

Customs inspectors work alongside the technology, assessing indicators of potential risk and directing inspections accordingly.

How Dubai’s iDeclare service works

Dubai Customs is also using digital services to streamline customs procedures for arriving passengers. Its smart iDeclare service works across a range of smart devices and allows travellers to declare personal belongings and accompanying gifts before they arrive.

According to Dubai Customs, the service can reduce the time needed to complete customs procedures through the red channel from 45 minutes to less than five minutes.

The digital process is also intended to reduce pressure on customs service points during peak travel periods.

Khalid Ahmed, Director of Passenger Operations at Dubai Customs, said: “We prepare for the return-season peak well in advance by analyzing flight schedules and passenger volumes. This allows us to deploy personnel and operational resources to the busiest areas at the right time. Our plan is built around round-the-clock operations, the optimal use of screening equipment and advanced technologies, and the expertise of our inspectors. This ensures we can accommodate the increase in arriving passengers while maintaining fast procedures and high-quality service.

“Operational efficiency during peak periods is measured not only by the volume of passengers we can handle, but also by how easy we make the journey for travelers and our ability to save them time and reduce procedures while maintaining border security and protecting the community. That is why we continue to invest in inspector expertise, develop digital tools, and use data and risk analysis to make inspections more targeted and effective. Our goal is for every arriving passenger to experience the level of service Dubai is known for from the moment they land.”

Dubai authorities coordinate during peak travel periods

Ahmed stressed that continuous coordination with Dubai Airports, the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai, Dubai Police, Emirates, flydubai and other airport partners is a key pillar of peak-period management.

The integrated approach is intended to allow authorities to respond flexibly to changes in flight volumes and coordinate the work of stakeholders involved in the passenger arrival process.

Dubai Customs is also participating as a strategic partner within oneDXB in the “Back to Dubai” celebration organised by Dubai Airports.

The initiative is welcoming returning residents and families as the new school year begins.

Dubai Customs said its wider approach combines technology, skilled personnel and partnerships as it responds to sustained growth in international travel and supports the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33.

title.rendered: Dubai property: 75% of 564,000 homes under construction already sold as villa demand hits 85%

content.rendered:
More than three-quarters of residential properties currently under construction in Dubai have already been sold, with buyers purchasing 425,863 of the 564,072 homes being built across the emirate, according to new market analysis.

The figures from fäm Properties show particularly high absorption rates for villas and for properties approaching completion, with 82.9 per cent of the 96,585 homes scheduled for delivery this year already sold.

There are currently 564,072 residential properties under construction across Dubai, with the majority scheduled for handover by 2028.

Of the total, 425,863 properties have already been sold, representing an overall absorption rate of 75.5 per cent.

Dubai has 564,072 homes under construction

Apartments account for the vast majority of the development pipeline, with 495,775 units under construction. Of those, 367,514 have been sold, giving apartments an absorption rate of 74.1 per cent.

Demand is higher among villas, with 58,349 of the 68,297 properties being built already sold — an absorption rate of 85.4 per cent.

Firas Al Msaddi, CEO of fäm Properties, said: “The fact that around three quarters of apartments and more than eight in ten villas currently under construction have already been sold reflects a market where demand keeps pace with development.

“Investors commit to buying properties before completion because they have confidence in Dubai, its transparent regulatory framework and the consistent quality being delivered by developers.

“Dubai’s population has now surpassed 4.58 million, and that it’s now home to more than 80,000 millionaires. All this reinforces Dubai’s position as one of the world’s most attractive destinations to live, work and invest.”

80,127 Dubai homes due in 2026 already sold

Absorption rates are even higher among homes approaching completion.

Of the 96,585 residential properties due to be delivered this year, 80,127 (82.9 per cent) have already been sold.

Dubai is scheduled to see 91,209 apartments delivered during the year, with an absorption rate of 82 per cent. For villas, the rate rises to 95 per cent across the 5,376 properties due for handover.

Data from DXBinteract shows some locations have reached 100 per cent absorption for properties scheduled for completion this year.

These include 637 apartments in Al Wasl, as well as 854 villas in Wadi Al Safa 5, 235 villas in Nad Al Sheba First and 476 villas in Al Hebiah Sixth.

Palm Jumeirah and JLT homes

High absorption rates are also being recorded in some of Dubai’s best-known residential areas.

On Palm Jumeirah, 93.5 per cent of the 2,397 apartments scheduled for delivery this year have already been sold. At Jumeirah Lakes Towers, 92.8 per cent of the 2,324 apartments due for completion this year have been purchased.

Downtown Dubai has 6,248 apartments under construction, with 92.2 per cent already sold.

Among the 3,981 Downtown Dubai apartments scheduled to be handed over in 2026, the absorption rate rises to 96.6 per cent.

Business Bay has more than 30,000 apartments under construction

Business Bay has 30,317 apartments currently under construction, of which 82.8 per cent have already been sold. Of the 16,938 Business Bay apartments scheduled for delivery this year, 88.7 per cent have been sold.

Other areas recording high absorption rates for apartments under construction include Ras Al Khor, where 93.5 per cent of 6,950 units have sold, and Al Barsha South 2, where the rate stands at 85 per cent across 12,655 apartments.

Several Dubai communities are recording particularly high absorption rates for villas currently under construction.

Al Hebiah Fifth has the highest rate among the locations highlighted in the analysis, with 98.7 per cent of 2,060 villas sold.

Nad Al Sheba First has recorded a 98.2 per cent absorption rate across 1,569 villas, while Wadi Al Safa 5 stands at 96.4 per cent across 8,216.

In Al Yufrah, 94.7 per cent of 6,429 villas under construction have been sold, while Dubai South has recorded a 94.5 per cent rate across 5,698 villas.

The figures show that high levels of off-plan sales extend across both apartments and villas, including projects scheduled for delivery this year and developments forming part of Dubai’s longer-term residential construction pipeline.

excerpt.rendered: More than 75% of Dubai homes under construction are already sold, with 425,863 of 564,072 properties purchased and villa absorption reaching 85.4%

title.rendered: Hong Kong’s new frontier: A safe harbour for Gulf capital

content.rendered:
Across the Gulf, the direction of capital is unmistakable. Sovereign wealth and private fortunes are diversifying east, and central banks worldwide are rebuilding their gold reserves as part of a move to diversify reserve assets. Even through this year’s sharp swings in the gold price, that structural shift has only accelerated – central banks are buying the dips at a historic pace, and a World Gold Council survey revealed that 89 per cent of global central banks expect official gold reserves to increase.

The lesson for reserve managers, sovereign investors and trading houses is clear: the story was never the day’s spot price – it is where to store, finance and settle physical metal safely in a fragmenting world.

That question is where the Gulf and Hong Kong meet. As the region’s own transformation – from Vision 2030 to the UAE‘s industrial and AI ambitions – reorients trade and investment toward Asia, the question for ambitious enterprises is no longer whether to engage Asia’s next decade of growth, but where to anchor, finance and scale that ambition.

A place to build, a market to plug into

Every enterprise expanding into Asia needs two things: a place to build, and a market to plug into. Hong Kong now offers both, side by side. The place is the Northern Metropolis – a 30,000-hectare canvas along the Mainland border, with innovation and technology at its core. The market is one of the world’s deepest pools of capital and trading infrastructure, increasingly geared to store, clear and finance the gold and real-economy flows moving through Asia. One gives you somewhere to operate; the other gives you the means to scale – and Gulf funds are already pivoting decisively toward the region.

The appetite is already visible. In July, Hong Kong hosted the inaugural LEAP East – the first edition of the flagship technology conference staged outside Saudi Arabia – drawing more than 35,000 participants from 30 countries and regions, and set to return for the next three years. Co-hosted by Saudi and Hong Kong government leaders, it underscored a deepening partnership and Hong Kong’s role as the gateway connecting the Chinese Mainland with the world.

The north engine: innovation and technology at the core

Spanning roughly one-third of Hong Kong’s land along the Shenzhen border, the Northern Metropolis is the “north engine” of a new dual-engine economy – innovation and industry in the north, finance and professional services in the south.

Across the Gulf, decision-makers will recognise the logic of state-backed mega-projects built to reshape an economic map – King Abdullah Economic City, vast districts anchored by long-term government commitment. The Northern Metropolis takes that logic further, and carries a distinct strength as it plugs directly into a mature international financial centre from day one, giving enterprises immediate access to world-class capital, professional services and global connectivity. The development has already progressed from the blueprint into delivery, with major projects now moving decisively from planning to implementation.

Innovation sits at its heart. The San Tin Technopole offers more than 200 hectares for R&D and new industrialisation across life sciences, AI, robotics and green tech, while the Hong Kong–Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park (HSITP) functions as a cross-border testbed facilitating the flow of talent, capital, data and goods. A new data-centre cluster at Sandy Ridge is strengthening the computing backbone for AI-driven industry, set to deliver a step-change in the city’s computing power over the coming years.

Land award weighting more for industry vision, not the highest bidder

Perhaps the clearest signal of intent is how land is awarded. In most great cities, prime land goes to the highest bidder; the Northern Metropolis flips that logic, with financial bidding counting for less than a third of the decision and the strength of the industry proposal – vision, speed, investment and jobs – counting for the rest. That door is already open: at Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen, the first large-scale land disposal has gone to tender, while pharmaceutical leader Pfizer has formed a strategic partnership at HSITP.

“The Greater Bay Area is one of the most dynamic economic regions on earth – a $2 trillion economy, 88 million consumers, and recently ranked by WIPO as the world’s leading innovation cluster,” said Mr Arnold Lau, Associate Director-General of Investment Promotion. “For Gulf investors and enterprises, the Northern Metropolis is the doorway into that ecosystem – a base running on Hong Kong’s common law system and the free flow of capital, talent and data, minutes from the Mainland’s manufacturing and research strength. That is the essence of Hong Kong’s evolution from super-connector to super value-adder.”

From super-connector to global gold and commodities hub

That innovation base is matched by Hong Kong’s fast-emerging strength as a global hub for gold and commodities, a policy-backed build-out explicitly supported under China’s 15th Five-Year Plan. And the timing speaks directly to the Gulf: precisely because this year has shown how volatile the gold price can be, the value of secure, well-governed infrastructure to hold physical metal has never been clearer – and official institutions have kept accumulating through every dip.

Gold storage is the entry point, and Hong Kong is assembling the entire chain. In July 2026, a government-owned central clearing and settlement system for gold entered trial operation, with the first physical gold deposited and the first trades completed. It launched alongside an initial Delivery Connect link with the Shanghai Gold Exchange, connecting the two markets for two-way physical flows. Storage capacity is targeted to exceed 2,000 tonnes within three years, and a 50 per cent profits-tax concession for eligible commodity traders is now before the legislature. For Gulf investors and trading houses managing reserves and cross-border settlement, it adds up to a trusted, common-law jurisdiction at the doorstep of the world’s largest demand centre – with 32 hectares in Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen reserved for a modern logistics cluster to serve those flows.

Your foothold in Asia’s next decade

For Gulf enterprises, sovereign investors and trading houses, the Northern Metropolis is more than Hong Kong’s next development – it is your access point to Asia’s next decade of trade, capital and innovation, and a secure, internationally governed home for gold and commodities. The early movers will shape this ecosystem. InvestHK stands ready as your on-the-ground partner, connecting you to the right sites, licensing, talent and capital.

To find your place in Hong Kong’s new frontier, contact InvestHK at enq@investhk.gov.hk.

title.rendered: UAE schools share update ahead of new term following recent missile alerts

content.rendered:
UAE schools are set to open as planned on 31 August for the 2026-27 academic year, despite a missile alert issued on 18 August, school leaders have said.

School leaders say no new guidance has been issued by authorities, with existing safety protocols remaining sufficient for the new term.

As campuses prepare to welcome more than a million pupils, principals said there had been no changes to opening arrangements following the alert.

School leaders say it is ‘business as usual’

Michael Strachan, head of the secondary school at Arcadia British School, said the existing safety procedures would not affect the return-to-school experience for children.

“The key thing is business as usual. We have a wonderful set-up for our emergency procedures. The likelihood of anything impacting us is incredibly small,” he said.

“Yes, we have to be mindful of the region and what is happening. That shouldn’t have a negative impact on the overall experience of the children in the school. Yes, we are prepared, in the same way we do fire drills and lockdown drills … we have them in place just in case.”

An underground hall, car park and additional rooms at Arcadia British School provide ready-made evacuation spaces for pupils and staff.

“We are lucky that a significant amount of our infrastructure is underground,” Mr Strachan said, referring to a multi-purpose hall and a large underground car park serving both the secondary and primary sections. “That means we have a ready-made evacuation place so we can shelter under the building if we need.”

He added staff and pupils would spend time refreshing safety drills that have been in place since the conflict began on 28 February, calling the procedures part of KHDA-mandated safety requirements. New and returning staff would go through refresher training, he said, with drills for children once term resumes.

Stephen Davis, vice principal of Repton School Abu Dhabi, said nothing had changed compared with the previous year.

“At the moment, nothing is different for us from last year,” he said. “We have obviously got really thorough procedures in place which will continue from last academic year. So it’s really just about refining those and ensuring everything is as smooth as possible.”

Jon Hughes, head teacher of the Senior School at Repton School Abu Dhabi, said the school was ready to welcome pupils and parents back, with online learning available as a fallback if needed.

“We don’t expect anything (new) but to have our students back in the building, our parents back in the building. If required, we have a wonderful online provision and are ready to revert to it at any time. But we are 100 per cent ready to have everyone back in the building,” he said.

John Bagust, director of education and executive principal for the Pace Group of Schools in Dubai and Sharjah, said his schools were continuing with the security measures already in place. “I have not had either KHDA or SPEA give additional guidance regarding the security aspect,” he said.

“For us it’s kind of business as usual, and it’s just really looking forward to hopefully a really smooth academic year coming up,” Mr Davis added.

Safety protocols

Existing emergency measures include shelter-in-place procedures, designated safe zones, strict campus access controls and online learning contingencies.

The protocols date back to April, when UAE schools resumed in-person learning after weeks of remote learning, reopening with enhanced safety measures including mandatory shelter-in-place procedures and blue-taped safe zones under nationwide regulations. Campus access controls, staff training and the suspension of large gatherings were also introduced at the time.

School leaders said the measures form part of existing emergency and business continuity plans, which include moving pupils and staff to designated safe areas away from windows and exposed locations, restricting movement on campus, taking attendance, and maintaining communication with parents.

Schools are required to follow official guidance and keep pupils on site until authorities confirm it is safe to resume normal activity.
